The DURABLE contract is the tier vocabulary + the routing rubric in Superscalar.md §5.1; this file carries only the perishable part (which concrete models occupy which tier today, and what each vendor actually accepts as an effort value). Replace the data, keep the vocabulary. Every row is expected to carry a confirmedBy URL — an unverifiable claim belongs in caveats[], not in models[].
method: Six-axis live-source sweep (Anthropic / OpenAI / Google+xAI / open-weight / benchmarks / harness binding), each axis independently fact-checked by an adversarial pass instructed to refute; only vendor-page-confirmed ids and values were promoted here. Corrections applied included one fabricated model id, one shut-down model presented as current, and several mis-attributed benchmark sources. 2026-08-01 structural adjustment (not a data re-sweep): the T1.5 · Frontier Execution band was split out of T1 — the 2026-07-25 sweep recorded the 2x intra-T1 price spread ($10/$50 vs $5/$25) but the tier boundary absorbed it, and a temperament axis (think-to-action latency) surfaced in dogfood that the price rows do not carry. claude-opus-5 moved T1 → T1.5, and a per-account entitlement-check rule was added for invitation-gated models (claude-mythos-5).

revisit.trigger: 2026-09-01 is chosen because it is the first date on which a SINGLE revisit re-baselines every dated event in the near window: Opus 4.1's 2026-08-05 retirement, OpenAI's 2026-08-10 chat-latest shutdowns, and Sonnet 5's 2026-08-31 introductory-pricing expiry all land before it, so pricing and id-validity can be re-derived in one pass rather than three. It also matches the observed cadence: Anthropic shipped Fable 5 (2026-06-09), Sonnet 5 (2026-06-30) and Opus 5 (2026-07-24) — 21 and 24 days apart; OpenAI shipped GPT-5.4 (2026-03-05), 5.5 (2026-04-24) and 5.6 (2026-07-09); Google shipped 3.1 Flash-Lite (2026-05-07), 3.5 Flash (2026-05-19) and the 3.6 Flash wave (2026-07-21); Moonshot shipped K3 (2026-07-16) and DeepSeek V4 (2026-04-24). Across the five vendors something material lands roughly every two to three weeks, and per-vendor flagships land every five to eight weeks — so ~5.5 weeks is about one flagship generation of drift, the most staleness this registry can absorb before a tier row is wrong. FORCE AN EARLIER REVISIT, do not wait for 2026-09-01, on any of: (a) 2026-08-05, to confirm nothing in the estate still pins claude-opus-4-1-20250805; (b) 2026-07-27, to check whether Kimi K3 weights actually published, since that single event is what makes a frontier-tier self-hosted lane real; (c) any new flagship announcement from Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, because Opus 5 shipped ONE DAY before this sweep and the whole T1 row would move again; (d) the first observed silent effort clamp or model substitution in a scripted run, which indicates an org-policy or alias-resolution change this registry cannot see; (e) any harness upgrade (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok Build), since several findings here are version-gated — Opus 5 needs v2.1.219+, org effort limits v2.1.195+, ultracode v2.1.203+, the 20-subagent limit v2.1.217+.

tiers.definition: The vendor's deepest-reasoning flagship, highest cost per token, thinking on by default and often not disableable. Characterized by sustained multi-hour autonomy, self-verification before acting, and the widest reasoning-effort ladder (including a top rung the cheaper tiers lack). Today: claude-fable-5, gpt-5.6-sol, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, grok-4.5, kimi-k3; gated members: claude-mythos-5 (restricted access), gpt-5.5-pro (escalation-only).
tiers.selectionIntent: Select when the cost of a wrong answer exceeds the cost of the tokens: irreversible actions, ambiguous or under-specified inputs, architecture that later work will be built on, and adversarial review of another model's output. Do NOT select for volume — its per-token price is the tier's defining constraint, and vendor guidance is that a larger model can be cheaper per finished task only when the task is genuinely hard.

tiers.definition: The vendor's start-here flagship: frontier-class capability at roughly half T1 per-token price, positioned by the vendor itself as the default for complex agentic coding rather than for deepest deliberation. Split from T1 on temperament as much as price: it converts thinking into action sooner — speed on well-framed work, a slip risk on under-framed work. Today: claude-opus-5. Vendors without a separate id here may span the band with a mode switch instead (gpt-5.6-sol reasoning.mode standard|pro) — such rows stay in T1 until measured.
tiers.selectionIntent: Select for complex multi-step execution where judgment remains but the frame is already set: the daily-driver main loop, heavyweight implementation lanes, subagent leads. Always pair it with explicit verification gates (check-first, test gates) — the observed failure mode is premature action, and raising effort does not buy deliberation here. Escalate to T1 for architecture, ambiguous requirements, and adversarial review; drop to T2 once the spec is complete. Not a verification tier: adversarial review stays T1, cross-family.

tiers.definition: The workhorse: near-frontier coding capability at roughly a third to a half of T1 per-token cost, tuned for tool loops and multi-file edits, with a full effort ladder and a large (≥400K, usually ~1M) context window. Today: claude-sonnet-5 / claude-opus-4-8, gpt-5.6-terra, gemini-3.6-flash / gemini-3.5-flash, grok-4.3, glm-5.2, deepseek-v4-pro.
tiers.selectionIntent: The default tier for the main coding loop once the decision is already made and the spec is written. Select whenever the work is 'do the thing correctly' rather than 'decide what the thing is'. This is where a maintainer should spend most tokens; escalation to T1 should be the exception you can name a reason for.

tiers.definition: Cheap-but-competent models the vendor itself markets for subagents and fan-out — real code edits and real tool use, but a smaller window or a shallower reasoning ceiling than T2. Typically 5-15x cheaper on output than T1. Today: gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.4-mini, grok-build-0.1, deepseek-v4-flash.
tiers.selectionIntent: Select for wide parallel lanes where the unit of work is small, independently verifiable, and cheap to redo: read-heavy scans, large-file review, per-file mechanical edits, test scaffolding. The economic point of this tier is that a failed lane is cheap to re-run, so buy width instead of depth.

tiers.definition: The cheapest always-on tier: sub-$1 input, minimal or off-by-default thinking, lowest latency floor. Marketed for classification, extraction, routing and watch loops rather than authoring. Often has NO effort parameter at all (claude-haiku-4-5) or defaults to none/minimal (gpt-5.4-nano, gemini-3.5-flash-lite, gemini-2.5-flash-lite). Today: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, gpt-5.4-nano, gemini-3.5-flash-lite / gemini-3.1-flash-lite / gemini-2.5-flash-lite.
tiers.selectionIntent: Select for anything that must run continuously and mostly return 'nothing to do': inbox/board polling, event classification, triage routing, digest extraction. Budget it as a fixed monthly cost, not per-task. Never let this tier author code or make a routing decision that is expensive to reverse — its job is to decide whether to wake a higher tier.

Best for tasks larger than one sitting. Vendor effort guidance: "Lower effort settings on Claude Fable 5 still perform well and often exceed xhigh performance on prior models" — so step DOWN here before stepping across tiers. models.notes: Vendor: "For complex agentic coding and enterprise work"; the model the docs tell you to start with. Released 2026-07-24 (one day before this sweep). Vendor effort guidance is explicit: "use low and medium liberally as your primary control for token cost and response time wherever your evals show quality holds", and "If you carried effort settings over from an earlier model, run a fresh effort sweep". Caution for agent harnesses: effort does NOT reliably shorten visible responses on Opus 5 — prompt for length instead. Knowledge cutoff May 2026. Repositioned T1 → T1.5 on 2026-08-01 from dogfood observation (single maintenance workspace, NOT vendor-confirmed): it converts thinking into action sooner than Fable 5, with a higher slip rate on multi-step work — pair a main loop on this model with explicit verification gates (check-first / test gates), and escalate decisions and adversarial review to T1 rather than raising effort, since effort does not reliably buy deliberation here (see the caution above).

The only cheap tier Anthropic sells — there is no Haiku 5, and at Feb 2025 knowledge cutoff it is the oldest model in the active lineup. 200K context and the total absence of an effort knob rule it out of long agentic loops; it is a watcher/classifier, not a coder. taskShapeRouting.effort: high (the default) — step to xhigh only when evals show headroom; reserve max for genuinely frontier problems
taskShapeRouting.why: Anthropic's own guidance is to "Pick a larger model when the problem is genuinely hard. For example, problems like subtle bugs, unfamiliar domains, or architecture decisions", and the effort docs pair that with starting at the default rather than the ceiling.

taskShapeRouting.effort: high, with xhigh when the ambiguity spans many files or tools
taskShapeRouting.why: Fable 5's documented strength is that it "investigates before acting" and self-verifies, which is precisely what an under-specified request needs; a cheaper tier will confidently resolve the ambiguity the wrong way and the error surfaces only after the code is written.

taskShapeRouting.taskShape: Complex multi-step execution with residual judgment (daily-driver main loop, heavyweight implementation lanes)
taskShapeRouting.effort: high (the default); do not raise effort to buy deliberation — pair with verification gates (check-first, test gates) instead
taskShapeRouting.why: The vendor positions claude-opus-5 as the start-here model for complex agentic coding at half T1 price; dogfood observation (2026-08-01) adds the boundary — it acts sooner than T1, so this band buys frontier capability for execution while decisions (architecture, ambiguity) and adversarial review stay on T1 and spec-complete work drops to T2.

taskShapeRouting.effort: high default; drop to medium once evals hold — on Sonnet 5 medium is "Comparable to Claude Sonnet 4.6 at high effort"
taskShapeRouting.why: Vendor guidance is to "Pick a smaller model when the work is routine. For example, edits you can describe precisely" — once the decision is made the remaining risk is execution fidelity, which T2 buys at a third to a half the per-token cost.

Vendor effort table puts low at "short, scoped, latency-sensitive tasks that are not intelligence-sensitive" and warns that max "is prone to overthinking" on structured-output work — a rote rename is exactly the shape where extra reasoning invents unrequested changes.

taskShapeRouting.effort: medium, raised to high when tests must infer intent rather than mirror a spec
taskShapeRouting.why: Test bodies are mostly mechanical once the contract is fixed, but choosing WHICH cases matter is a judgement step; medium keeps cost down while leaving enough reasoning to enumerate edge cases, and you raise effort only on the observed failure of missing them.

OpenAI's Codex subagent doc names this shape verbatim for its execution tier — "agents that favor speed and efficiency over depth, such as exploration, read-heavy scans, large-file review" — and Anthropic notes lower effort makes FEWER tool calls, which is the dominant cost term in a search lane.

taskShapeRouting.effort: low; none or minimal where the vendor offers it (gpt-5.4-nano defaults to none, gemini-3.5-flash-lite to minimal)
taskShapeRouting.why: Anthropic's effort docs list "simple classification tasks, quick lookups, or high-volume use cases" as the canonical low-effort case; reasoning adds cost without changing a well-specified extraction, and the cheap tiers already default to the right rung.

taskShapeRouting.effort: medium — the binding constraint is window and per-token price, not reasoning depth
taskShapeRouting.why: Every current T2 carries ~1M context, but the cost cliffs sit at different thresholds — >272K doubles input on the GPT-5.6 family, ≥200k doubles it on all Grok models and on gemini-3.1-pro-preview — so the routing decision here is which cliff you can stay under, and deepseek-v4-pro's $0.003625 cache-hit rate is the cheapest way to re-read the same corpus.

taskShapeRouting.effort: minimal or none; low only when the watcher must classify intent rather than match a pattern
taskShapeRouting.why: Google's changelog calls gemini-3.5-flash-lite "a low-latency, highly cost-effective subagent option" and ships it with thinking_level defaulting to "minimal" — the vendor has already tuned this tier for the wake-or-ignore loop, and the observer's only real decision is whether to escalate.

taskShapeRouting.effort: xhigh — "Deeper reasoning at higher token spend"
taskShapeRouting.why: Verification is the one shape where paying T1 rates on a small input is clearly worth it, because a missed defect is discovered downstream at far higher cost; running the verifier on the same model that authored the code correlates the blind spots, so cross-vendor separation is the point, not a nicety.

effortGuidance: Default first, escalate on evidence — not on principle. Anthropic's own Claude Code guidance is "For most tasks you should use the model's default effort level", and to "Pick a higher effort level if Claude got it wrong by skipping a file, not running the tests, or not double-checking its work." Escalation should be traceable to an observed failure mode, not to the importance of the task.

NON-MONOTONICITY IS VENDOR-DOCUMENTED, not folklore. Claude Code's effort table says of max: "Can improve performance on demanding tasks but may show diminishing returns and is prone to overthinking. Test before adopting broadly." The API docs are blunter for the Opus 4.7/4.8 line: "On most workloads max adds significant cost for relatively small quality gains, and on some structured-output or less intelligence-sensitive tasks it can lead to overthinking." A blanket always-max policy is therefore a documented anti-pattern, not merely expensive.

Effort level names are NOT comparable across models: "The effort scale is calibrated per model, so the same level name does not represent the same underlying value across models." Any harness that stores one global effort setting and applies it to whatever model is active is storing a meaningless number — bind effort per model, as Claude Code does with per-subagent and per-skill `effort` frontmatter.

Carried-over settings are actively harmful after a model change. Anthropic on Opus 5: "If you carried effort settings over from an earlier model, run a fresh effort sweep on your evals rather than reusing them." This bites hardest in Claude Code, where Fable 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 HOLD their default effort until you make an explicit choice, but Opus 5 has no such hold — a level you set for another model silently carries over.

Step DOWN the ladder before stepping across tiers. Vendor guidance for Fable 5: "Lower effort settings on Claude Fable 5 still perform well and often exceed xhigh performance on prior models." And for Sonnet 5, medium is "Comparable to Claude Sonnet 4.6 at high effort." A generation bump usually means the cheap rung of the new model beats the expensive rung of the old one — check that before downgrading tier.

Low effort is the intended subagent setting, and it changes tool behavior, not just prose. The effort docs list low's typical use as "Simpler tasks that need the best speed and lowest costs, such as subagents", and state that lower effort makes the model "Combine multiple operations into fewer tool calls" and "Make fewer tool calls". In a search or exploration lane, tool-call count is the dominant cost term, so low effort saves more than the token delta suggests.

Effort is a behavioral signal, not a token budget: "At lower effort levels, Claude will still think on sufficiently difficult problems, but it will think less than it would at higher effort levels for the same problem." You cannot use effort as a hard cost cap — pair it with max_tokens, and conversely at xhigh/max the docs tell you to set a LARGE max_tokens ("Starting at 64k tokens") or the model runs out of room mid-thought.

Effort is a caching decision as much as a quality decision: "Changing the effort value between requests invalidates prompt caching, so vary effort across workloads rather than within a conversation that relies on cache hits." For a long resident session, pick one level at session start and hold it; dynamic per-turn effort tuning can cost more than it saves.

On Opus 5, do not use effort to control verbosity — "changing effort does not reliably shorten responses, so prompt for length instead." Harnesses that lowered effort to cut output size on older models will see the cost saving without the brevity, and Opus 5 is separately reported to narrate more than 4.8 by default.

Know the two default-effort exceptions before you trust a default. In Claude Code "The default effort is high on every model that supports effort, except Opus 4.7, which defaults to xhigh." On the OpenAI side the exception runs the other way: gpt-5.4-mini and gpt-5.4-nano default reasoning.effort to `none`, so omitting the parameter gives you a non-reasoning model on a code-editing lane.

Anthropic's cheap tier has NO effort knob at all: claude-haiku-4-5 rejects the effort parameter and has no adaptive thinking. That asymmetry is a routing constraint, not a detail — if your resident-observer lane needs a dial, Google's Flash-Lite line (minimal/low/medium/high) or gpt-5.4-nano gives you one and Haiku does not.

On Google, effort control is now the ONLY supported determinism knob: the 2026-07-21 changelog deprecated temperature, top_p and top_k in the Gemini API. Any harness pinning temperature for reproducible output must migrate to thinking_level.

xAI has no low end of the ladder: for grok-4.5 the values are low, medium, high (default high) and "Reasoning cannot be disabled" — there is no none/minimal rung, so xAI cannot serve a true resident-observer lane on effort alone. Separately, on grok-4.20-multi-agent, effort selects AGENT COUNT (4 or 16) rather than reasoning depth, which makes xhigh there a 16x token multiplier rather than a deeper single pass.

`ultracode` and `ultrathink` are not effort levels and should not be modelled as such. Ultracode "is a Claude Code setting rather than a model effort level: it sends xhigh to the model and additionally has Claude orchestrate dynamic workflows", is session-only, and is rejected by both the persisted effortLevel setting and CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL. Ultrathink "adds an in-context instruction" and "The effort level sent to the API is unchanged" — so it costs nothing at the API-parameter layer and changes nothing there either.
planGating: Claude Code — Pro: `default` resolves to Sonnet 5. Opus 5 IS selectable (Anthropic calls it "the strongest model on Claude Pro"), but Opus with the 1M window "Requires usage credits" on Pro — it is included with subscription only on Max/Team/Enterprise. Sonnet 4.6 at 1M needs credits on every plan including Max.

Claude Code — Max (5x/20x) and Team Premium seats: `default` resolves to Opus 5 ("Max, Team Premium, Enterprise pay-as-you-go, and Anthropic API: defaults to Opus 5"). Opus is auto-upgraded to 1M context with no configuration. Fable 5 is never the default on any account type — reach it via /model fable or the `best` alias where the org has access, and it is hidden entirely under zero data retention.

Claude Code — Team Standard and Enterprise subscription seats: `default` resolves to Sonnet 5, not Opus 5 ("Pro, Team Standard, and Enterprise subscription seats: defaults to Sonnet 5"). Enterprise pay-as-you-go orgs get Opus 5. Seat billing tier, not company size, decides the tier an agent starts on.

Claude Code — Enterprise governance: admins can disable individual models org-wide or per custom role (Haiku can never be disabled, so every member always retains one usable model), set an organization default model that replaces the account-type default, and — Enterprise only — set a MAXIMUM EFFORT LEVEL PER MODEL PER ROLE. Levels above the cap vanish from the /effort picker and --effort requests run at the cap; the clamp warns in interactive and plain --print runs but "with json or stream-json output or in background agents, the clamp applies silently." A scripted agent can therefore run below its requested effort with no signal.

Claude Code — Anthropic API key: `default` resolves to Opus 5, full lineup available, `opus`→Opus 5 / `sonnet`→Sonnet 5 / `best`→Fable 5 where entitled. No subscription cap; org TPM/RPM limits apply, and Opus 5 draws on a separate rate-limit bucket from the combined Opus 4.x pool.

Claude Code — third-party providers are a generation behind on aliases: on Microsoft Foundry `default` resolves to Sonnet 4.5, and the `opus` alias still resolves to Opus 4.6 there. Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform resolved `default` to Sonnet 4.5 before v2.1.207. Organization effort limits are NOT delivered on Bedrock/Google Cloud/Foundry/Claude Platform on AWS — use availableModels in managed settings instead.

Claude Code — subagent model resolution order (this is where a tiered-composition policy actually lands): CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL → per-invocation `model` parameter → subagent frontmatter `model` → main conversation's model. Frontmatter accepts sonnet/opus/haiku/fable, a full id, or `inherit` (the default), and a separate `effort` frontmatter field overrides the session level while that subagent runs. Note the built-in Explore agent no longer forces Haiku: as of v2.1.198 it inherits the main model, capped at Opus on the Claude API — define a project subagent named Explore with `model: haiku` to put exploration back on a cheap lane. Concurrency default is 20 subagents per session (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS), and ultracode sessions are exempt from that limit.

Claude Code — fast mode: Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 only, at $10/$50 per MTok for up to ~2.5x output tokens/sec. Heavily gated: an API research preview needing the fast-mode-2026-02-01 beta header plus account-manager/waitlist access; in Claude Code it requires usage credits turned on, draws from credits from the first token even when plan usage remains, needs Owner enablement on Team/Enterprise, is CLI-only (not the VS Code extension), and is unavailable on Bedrock/Google Cloud/Foundry/Claude Platform on AWS. Enable at session start — the first enable re-bills the whole context at fast-mode uncached input price. Opus 4.7 fast mode was REMOVED 2026-07-24 while Claude Code still treats 4.7 as fast-mode-capable, so /fast on 4.7 produces API rejections.

Codex — Plus ($20/mo): gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.5, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini. Roughly 15-90 Sol messages per 5-hour window scaling to ~60-350 on Luna. This is the tier where Sol-on-every-lane is not viable — a wide fan-out must run Terra or Luna.

Codex — Pro ($100/mo 5x, $200/mo 20x): everything on Plus plus gpt-5.3-codex-spark (research preview, Pro only, ChatGPT-surfaces only, separately rate-limited). ~75-450 Sol messages (5x) to ~300-1,800 (20x) per 5-hour window — the first tier with real headroom for many-subagent operation.

Codex — Business ($25/user/mo, min 2): the same roster as Plus, WITHOUT codex-spark, and it does not inherit Pro's 5x/20x multipliers — a Business seat has Plus-sized headroom for fan-out. A common planning error is assuming the paid-team tier buys concurrency.

Codex — Enterprise/Edu and bring-your-own-key: model availability "follows the API models available to your key"; flexible-pricing workspaces have no fixed rate limits and scale with credits. With a BYO key you "Pay only for the tokens Codex uses, based on API pricing" — the ceiling becomes org rate limits and budget rather than a 5-hour window, which is the only configuration where per-lane model choice is a pure cost question.

Codex — per-agent binding (the mechanism a tiered policy needs): agent files at ~/.codex/agents/<name>.toml or .codex/agents/<name>.toml take `model` and `model_reasoning_effort`, and "If a custom agent file sets model or model_reasoning_effort, the value in the file takes precedence." Global [agents] keys: enabled (default true), max_concurrent_threads_per_session, default_subagent_model, default_subagent_reasoning_effort. Session controls: /model, /effort, --model/-m, --reasoning-effort/-e.

Gemini CLI — maximum model requests per user per day: Gemini Code Assist (Individual) 1,000; Google AI Pro 1,500; Google AI Ultra 2,000; Code Assist Standard 1,500; Code Assist Enterprise 2,000; Gemini API key free/unpaid 250 and "Model requests to Flash model only"; paid API key and Vertex "Varies". Two things matter for agent design: one prompt can be dozens of model requests, and model availability is "across the Gemini model family as determined by Gemini CLI" — per-model selection is not plan-gated, the CLI chooses.

Gemini CLI — model selection lags the API materially. The CLI's valid-model set does not include gemini-3.6-flash or gemini-3.5-flash-lite, still hardcodes gemini-2.5-pro as DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL (a model with an announced 2026-10-16 shutdown) and gemini-3-pro-preview in its picker (shut down 2026-03-09). Selection surfaces: --model/-m (highest precedence) → GEMINI_MODEL → project settings → user settings; per-subagent via agents.overrides.<agentName>.modelConfig.model, since /model "does not override the model used by sub-agents".

xAI / Grok Build CLI — plan gating is NOT documented on any reachable xAI page: x.ai/news and x.ai/build/changelog return 403 to fetchers and docs.x.ai/build/overview states no subscription requirement. Beta access reportedly opened 2026-05-14 to SuperGrok Heavy then 2026-05-25 to all SuperGrok and X Premium+, with no public per-day quota table — usage is observable only in-session via /usage. Treat every Grok plan number as secondary-sourced.

Consumer Gemini app — Free gets gemini-3.6-flash as the new default plus a limited daily allotment of 3.1 Pro; AI Pro (~$19.99) adds Gemini 3 Pro access and Antigravity at basic limits (4x free limits); AI Ultra adds Deep Think / Gemini Spark at up to 20x Pro limits. Relevant only as a signal of which model a non-API teammate is actually talking to.

harnessBinding.perLaneModel: Agent tool per-invocation `model`; subagent frontmatter `model` (sonnet|opus|haiku|fable | full id | `inherit`, the default); resolution order = `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` env pin → per-invocation `model` → frontmatter `model` → main conversation model.
harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: subagent frontmatter `effort` (overrides the session level while that subagent runs); session-level `--effort` at launch · `/effort` · `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`. There is no per-subagent *thinking* setting.
harnessBinding.concurrency: default 20 subagents per session (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`); ultracode sessions are exempt from that limit.
caveats: Default effort is high on every effort-capable model except Opus 4.7 (xhigh).
Fable 5 / Opus 4.8 / Opus 4.7 hold a first-run default-effort choice across sessions that a non-interactive `/effort` cannot release (reports `Not applied`) — pass `--effort` at launch instead.
The env pin overrides even per-invocation choices and an org-allowlist-excluded value falls back to the inherited model silently — prefer per-invocation binding and verify actual application.
The built-in Explore agent no longer forces Haiku (inherits the main model since v2.1.198) — define a project subagent named Explore with `model: haiku` to put exploration back on a cheap lane.

Enterprise admins can cap maximum effort per model per role; with json/stream-json output or in background agents the clamp applies SILENTLY, so a scripted lane can run below its requested effort with no signal.

harnessBinding.perLaneModel: agent files at `~/.codex/agents/<name>.toml` or `.codex/agents/<name>.toml` with `model`; global `[agents] default_subagent_model`.
harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: same agent file with `model_reasoning_effort`; global `[agents] default_subagent_reasoning_effort`; session `/model`, `--model/-m`, `--reasoning-effort/-e`.
caveats: Precedence: a custom-agent file value wins; otherwise explicit spawn value → the `[agents]` default → the parent value.

Effort value sets differ across vendor pages (subagents page lists low..max/ultra; config reference lists minimal..xhigh) — treat the exact allowed set as per-model and verify against the model you bind.

harnessBinding.perLaneModel: subagent frontmatter — only `name`, `description`, `model` (default `inherit`), `readonly`, `is_background`. Bracket-option syntax carries the knobs: `composer-2.5[fast=false]`, `claude-opus-5[effort=high,context=300k]`.
harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: via the bracket parameter `effort` (also `fast`, `context`) — no separate effort field.
caveats: Auto Cost bills a flat per-million rate independent of the model that serves the request; Auto Balance / Auto Intelligence bill at the actual model rates and third-party models add a Cursor Token Rate.
Max Mode "API rate plus 20%" is scoped to legacy request-based plans only.

harnessBinding.perLaneModel: `agents.overrides.<agentName>.modelConfig.model` — `/model` does NOT change the model used by subagents. Selection precedence for the main lane: `--model/-m` → `GEMINI_MODEL` → project settings → user settings.
harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: no harness-level effort tier. Per-lane budget dials are the subagent schema fields instead: `kind`, `tools`, `mcpServers`, `temperature`, `max_turns`, `timeout_mins`.
harnessBinding.concurrency: not documented as a single key; day quotas are per plan (see planGating).
caveats: The CLI's valid-model set lags the API materially — it can still default to and offer models the API has shut down. Pin explicitly rather than trusting the picker.
Google deprecated temperature / top_p / top_k in the Gemini API (2026-07-21 changelog), leaving thinking_level as the determinism knob.

harnessBinding.perLaneModel: `[secondary_model]` — a second model pointer beside `default_model`, intended for spawning subagents at lower cost; accepts `model`, `default_effort` and the same patch fields as model overrides.
harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: `default_effort` on the model pointer; K3 accepts `reasoning_effort` low|high|max (default high).
caveats: `model_preference` accepts only `primary`/`secondary` — it never names a concrete model alias, so a lane picks a *pointer*, not a model.
Docs warn that K3 / K2.7 without Thinking routes to K2.6 — a silent cross-model reroute.

harnessBinding.perLaneModel: per-agent model selection exists in opencode; routers expose whatever the upstream provider accepts.
harnessBinding.perLaneEffort: unverified. opencode documents `reasoningEffort` only as a provider passthrough example, and LiteLLM does not explicitly document pinning `reasoning_effort` per deployment.
caveats: Treat per-lane effort at the router layer as unproven until measured on the actual provider+model pair.

A maintainer wanting a Qwen lane must confirm ids on DashScope directly.

LONG-CONTEXT SURCHARGE THRESHOLDS ARE A ROUTING HAZARD THAT VARIES BY VENDOR AND IS EASY TO MISS. GPT-5.6 family and gpt-5.4: prompts >272K input tokens are billed at 2x input and 1.5x output FOR THE FULL REQUEST (confirmed on the Sol, Terra and Luna model pages, though absent from the pricing table). All Grok text models: requests reaching 200k are billed at the higher rate for ALL tokens. gemini-3.1-pro-preview and gemini-2.5-pro: price break at 200k. Anthropic: no premium beyond 200K on the 1M window. A fan-out sized by nominal per-token price will overrun budget on three of four vendors.

FAST MODE MUST NOT BE MODELLED AS A SIMPLE PRICE TIER. It is an API research preview requiring the fast-mode-2026-02-01 beta header plus account-manager or waitlist access, and in Claude Code it additionally requires usage credits on, Owner enablement for Team/Enterprise, is CLI-only, is unavailable on Bedrock/Google Cloud/Foundry/Claude Platform on AWS, draws from credits from the first token even when plan usage remains, and re-bills the entire context at fast-mode uncached input price on first enable in a conversation. Opus 4.7 fast mode was removed 2026-07-24 while Claude Code still advertises it, so /fast on 4.7 produces API rejections.

CONTENT-BASED AUTOMATIC MODEL FALLBACK CAN CHANGE YOUR TIER WITHOUT ASKING, and it is directly relevant to security-adjacent repos. Fable 5: biology-flagged → re-runs on Opus 5; cybersecurity-flagged → Opus 4.8. Opus 5: cybersecurity-flagged → Opus 4.8; biology-flagged → refusal with no fallback. A flagged request can trip on the FIRST request from CLAUDE.md content or git status alone, and after fallback the session STAYS on the fallback model. If availableModels blocks the fallback target, no fallback happens and the request simply refuses. Requires v2.1.219+; `claude --safe-mode` isolates whether local customizations are the trigger.

GEMINI'S 2026-07-21 DEPRECATION OF temperature, top_p AND top_k IS A BREAKING CHANGE FOR ANY HARNESS THAT PINS THEM, and Gemini CLI docs still expose them via generateContentConfig. Migrate to thinking_level. Note also that the Gemini CLI caps thinking at 8192 tokens (DEFAULT_THINKING_MODE) to prevent runaway loops — an independent ceiling on the CLI path that the API path does not have.

evidenceContract.confirmedWhen: evidence 에 A 또는 B 가 1건 이상 있거나, **서로 다른 도메인**의 C/D 가 2건 이상. E 는 단독으로 confirmed 를 만들지 못해요. **반증이 확증을 이겨요** — `stance:"contradicts"` 인 A/B 가 1건이라도 있으면(또는 서로 다른 도메인 C/D 2건) status 는 refuted 예요. 근거가 갈리는 걸 confirmed 로 두면 그건 「반대 증거를 못 본 척」이에요.
evidenceContract.unconfirmedIsKept: 근거가 모자란 주장은 지우지 않고 status unconfirmed 로 남겨요. 지우면 다음 조사가 같은 자리를 처음부터 다시 발견해야 하고, 통과시키면 근거 없는 것이 근거 있는 것처럼 굴어요.
evidenceContract.neverAct: unconfirmed 주장은 하네스 구성을 바꾸는 근거로 쓰지 않아요. 조사 대상 목록일 뿐이에요.
evidenceContract.researchMethod: 신뢰 자료(공급사 문서·모델 카드·엔지니어 발화·벤치)를 기본으로 하고, 그 위에 커뮤니티·SNS 보고를 **합산 신호**로 얹어요. 접근 제약이 있는 표면은 별도 조사 도구를 씁니다. 축당 1패스로 넓게 훑고, 강한 주장만 교차검증으로 좁혀요.
evidenceContract.refutedIsKept: 반증된 주장도 지우지 않아요. 지우면 「아직 안 봤음」과 구분이 안 되고, 다음 조사가 같은 자리를 처음부터 다시 발견해요. 남기되 구성 근거로 쓰지 않아요.

harnessProfile.key: apiModelId × effort. effort 이름은 모델 사이에 비교가 안 되고(공급사가 명시), 낮은 effort 는 도구 호출 방식 자체를 바꿔요(적게·묶어서) — 그래서 같은 모델이라도 effort 에 따라 덜어낼 것이 달라져요. effort "*" 는 «그 모델 전체» 를 뜻해요.

shed.claim: 검증 장치 — 「마지막에 검증 단계를 넣어라」 · 「다시 확인해라」 · 검증 전용 서브에이전트
shed.why: 스스로 검증해요. 지시를 남겨 두면 자기 거동과 겹쳐서 과잉검증이 되고, 토큰만 쓰고 품질은 안 올라요. 공급사가 **레거시 하네스 스캐폴딩**까지 이름 대서 같은 판정을 내렸어요.

evidence.note: 「verifies its own work without being told to … remove them … The same applies to legacy harness scaffolding that adds separate verification steps」 + 「Avoid instructing re-checks it already performs」 + 「do not use subagents to verify or double-check your own work」
「It also verifies its own work without being told to, so remove verification instructions carried over from earlier models … they cause over-verification」

shed.claim: 맥락 재주입 장치 — 긴 작업 중간에 앞의 지시를 다시 넣어 주던 부류
shed.why: **반증됨.** 지시 «따르기» 자체는 1M 창 전체에서 안 흔들린다고 문서가 말하지만, 같은 문서가 **긴 시스템 프롬프트에서는 프롬프트 끝에 짧은 리마인더를 한 번 더 붙이라고 권장**해요(톤 항목). 원 주장이 틀렸다기보다 **뭉뚱그려졌어요** — 지시 준수는 안 새고, 톤은 끝에서 다시 집어야 해요. 재주입을 통째로 덜면 톤이 흘러요.

evidence.note: 「In a long system prompt, pair the instruction with a short reminder near the end of the prompt」 — 즉 재주입을 권장. 한편 「instruction following, tool calling, and reasoning stay consistent throughout the window」 는 지시 감쇠는 없다는 쪽

prop.claim: 지탱할 것 — 범위 제약 · 나레이션 억제 · 위임 상한 · 길이 보정
prop.why: 기본 응답과 산출 문서가 길어지고, 나레이션이 잦고, 서브에이전트에 더 잘 위임하고, 요청보다 범위를 넓히는 경향이 있어요. 넷 다 **덜 게 아니라 붙일 것**이에요.

evidence.note: 「Response length and verbosity」·「User-facing progress updates」·「Controlling subagent spawning」·「Task scope and over-verification」 각 절의 권장 프롬프트

shed.claim: 예시 뭉치 — 문체·톤을 맞추려고 20개씩 넣던 부류
shed.why: 공급사 문서가 예시 **개수**를 다루지 않아요. 인접 항목(「기존 스킬이 이 모델엔 과도하게 처방적이라 품질을 떨어뜨릴 수 있으니 덜어 보라」)은 있지만 그건 *지시* 이야기지 *예시* 이야기가 아니에요 — 이웃 주장의 근거를 이 주장에 붙이지 않아요. 커뮤니티 합산(2차)에서 다시 봐요.

shed.claim: 추론 재현 지시 — 「생각한 과정을 응답에 적어라」류
shed.why: 이 모델에선 그런 지시가 **거부 범주를 유발**해서 다른 모델로의 폴백이 늘어요. 스킬·시스템 프롬프트에 남아 있으면 조용히 비용이 돼요. 우리 쪽 스킬도 감사 대상이에요.

evidence.note: 「Don't instruct Claude to reproduce its reasoning in the response … can trigger the reasoning_extraction refusal category … causing elevated fallbacks」

prop.claim: 지탱할 것 — **명시적 자기검증 + 신선한 문맥의 검증 서브에이전트**
prop.why: **Opus 5 와 정확히 반대예요.** 이 모델에는 자기검증을 명시하라고 하고, 자기비판보다 «신선한 문맥의 별도 검증 서브에이전트» 가 낫다고 해요. 같은 장치가 한 모델엔 지울 것이고 다른 모델엔 붙일 것 — 모델별 프로필이 필요한 이유가 추측이 아니라 문서 대조로 나온 자리예요.

evidence.note: 「Make self-verification explicit in long-run prompts. Separate, fresh-context verifier subagents tend to outperform self-critique.」 ↔ Opus 5 의 「do not use subagents to verify」 와 정반대

prop.claim: 지탱할 것 — 진행 주장을 도구 결과에 대조시키기 · 문맥 잔량 수치를 모델에 노출하지 않기
prop.why: 장기 자율 실행에서 진행 보고를 지어내는 경향이 있고, 남은 토큰 카운트다운을 보여 주면 스스로 새 세션을 제안하거나 작업을 줄여요.

evidence.note: 「Before reporting progress, audit each claim against a tool result … nearly eliminated fabricated status reports」 + 「Avoid surfacing explicit context-budget counts where possible」

advisorFor.why: **반증됨.** 공급사는 이 모델을 「가장 요구가 큰 추론과 장기 에이전틱 작업용」으로 자리매김해요 — 문체 모델이 아니에요. 오히려 프롬프팅 문서에 «사용자에게 읽히는 글» 을 위한 별도 교정 지침이 붙어 있어요(밀도 높은 축약·화살표 사슬을 쓰는 경향). 표현의 권위가 아니라 표현에 **도움이 필요한** 쪽이에요.

evidence.note: 「Anthropic's most capable widely released model, built for the most demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work」 — 문체·톤 특화라는 자리매김이 없음
「Readability when communicating with the user」 절 — 이 모델이 읽기 어려운 글을 내는 경향에 대한 완화 지침

avoidFor.role: 보안 점검 레인 — 공격자 시뮬레이션 · 레드팀 · 익스플로잇/공격도구 관련 작업
avoidFor.why: 이 모델의 안전 분류기가 **공격형 보안 기법**(익스플로잇·멀웨어·공격 도구 제작)을 겨냥하고, 문서가 **선의의 보안 작업도 걸릴 수 있다**고 명시해요. 우리 Ultrasafe 모듈은 스킬 이름부터 web-api-attacker · ai-llm-redteam · social-engineer 이고 관련 어휘가 138곳이라, 그 레인을 이 모델로 돌리면 체계적으로 거부→폴백이에요. 공급사 권장 완화도 폴백 구성이라, 애초에 그 레인을 여기로 안 보내는 게 맞아요. **적용 시점**: 8종 팬아웃은 2026-07-28 회차로 이미 한 번 돌았고(열린 발견 92건), 그 게이트는 resolved 예요 — 그러니 이건 **다음 회차(차단 모드 전환 심사)** 에 거는 제약이에요. 지난 회차가 영향받았는지는 **알 수 없어요**: 회차 원장이 시각·공격자 목록·해시만 들고 모델을 안 실어서, 어느 에이전트가 거절돼 폴백됐는지 사후 복원이 안 돼요.

evidence.note: 「safety classifiers that target offensive cybersecurity techniques (such as building exploits, malware, or attack tooling) … Benign cybersecurity work and beneficial life sciences tasks may also trigger these safeguards」 + 폴백 구성 권장
「Claude Fable 5 includes safety classifiers that can decline requests」 — refusal 은 200 응답으로 오고 어느 분류기가 거절했는지 보고됨

shed.claim: 판단 사안을 절대 규칙으로 굳힌 도구 사용 규칙 — 「질문에 '최신'이 있으면 검색하라」류
shed.why: 공급사가 **「when to search」를 판단 사안의 예시로 직접 이름 대면서** 절대 규칙 대신 decision rule 을 쓰라고 해요. 다만 「도구 규칙을 다 없애라」가 아니에요 — 안전·필수 필드 같은 **진짜 불변**에는 절대 규칙이 맞고, 판단 사안만 굳히지 말라는 거예요. 원 주장을 그 폭으로 좁혔어요.

evidence.note: 「Avoid unnecessary absolute rules. Use ALWAYS, NEVER, must, and only for true invariants … For judgment calls, such as when to search, ask, use a tool, or keep iterating, prefer decision rules.」

advisorFor.role: 교차 분석 — 다른 훈련 계보의 반박
advisorFor.why: 공급사 문서가 다룰 만한 주제가 아니에요(자기 모델을 남의 고문으로 권할 이유가 없어요). 근거를 찾으려면 커뮤니티·비교 벤치 쪽이라 2차 조사 대상이에요.

shed.claim: 승인 게이팅 — 단계를 쪼개 하나씩 사람 확인을 받게 하던 부류
shed.why: 세 계보 문서가 각각 같은 방향이에요. 모델이 이미 안정적으로 하는 거동에 절차 지시를 붙이지 말 것(OpenAI), 멈출 자리를 일일이 열거할 필요 없이 「정말 사람이 필요한 때만 멈춰라」 한 줄이면 됨(Fable), 범위는 제약하되 순서는 맡길 것(Opus). **검증 장치와 헷갈리지 마세요** — 그건 모델마다 반대예요.

evidence.note: 제거 대상 목록에 「process instructions for behavior the model already performs reliably」
「Pause for the user only when the work genuinely requires them … there is no need to enumerate every case」

harnessProfile.researchLog: 1차 조사(2026-08-02): 공급사 1차 문서 5종 정독. 확증 3 · **반증 2** · 미확정 2. 반증이 나온 게 이 계약의 값이에요 — 지웠으면 다음 조사가 같은 자리를 처음부터 다시 발견했을 거예요. 커뮤니티·SNS 합산은 아직 안 돌렸어요(공급사 문서만으로 A급이 나와서 2차로 미룸).
